open_points.subject: A18 startup orphan-value cleanup
open_points.text: “On start, temporary files, value bytes no record names … are removed” states no outcome when an unreferenced value-byte file cannot be inspected or removed; only failure to remove a spool directory is explicitly made non-fatal.
open_points.question: If an unreferenced value-byte file cannot be verified or removed at startup, does the kernel refuse to start, continue while leaving it unserved, or take another action?
options: Continue and leave the file unserved for a later start
Continue after recording or reporting a cleanup warning
open_points.default_guess: Refuse to start, because the explicit non-fatal exception applies only to spool-directory removal.

open_points.subject: A18 startup ordering and exclusive lock
open_points.text: Rule 1 says the kernel takes an exclusive lock “At start,” while the changed rule 4 says unreferenced value bytes are removed “On start,” without ordering the cleanup against lock acquisition, database inspection, sandbox checks, or A14 recovery.
open_points.question: At what exact point in startup is orphan-value discovery and removal performed, and must the exclusive data-directory lock and a stable committed database view be acquired first?
options: Acquire the exclusive lock and open/check the committed store, then clean orphan values before recovery
Clean orphan values before acquiring the lock
Acquire the lock, perform recovery, then clean orphan values before opening the surface
open_points.default_guess: Acquire the exclusive lock first, inspect a stable committed database to determine which bytes are named, clean the orphan values, and only then perform recovery and open the surface.
